bounce.verdict: Ollie hits Rex at 18.1 m/s and doesn’t slow: he takes his own recoil, so the push back from the hit goes to his source. Rex bounces off him and is sent off at 36.3 m/s, twice his speed, and slides 102 m.

happens: Momentum still balances, and canon says where it comes from. Ollie doesn’t slow, so everything Rex gains (110,000 kg·m/s) comes from Ollie’s source. That is canon’s case “their own recoil”: the push back from his own hit goes to his source. A perfect bounce frees no energy.“Immovable” only means what holds Rex in place. Against a charger who can’t slow, any hold with a limit gives: here his footing, 17.7 kN. Only a hold their powers make limitless can’t give (bolts on ground that Unbreakable footing keeps whole, or Unbreakable footing holding him up from below), and then there is no answer.In a perfect bounce Rex leaves him as the hit ends. Ollie never slows, so the lab has him stop himself then (his own push, so its push back, 54,400 kg·m/s, goes to his source too).How hard they hit depends on how squishy they are, which nobody knows for an indestructible plush. If they squash by a quarter of the smaller body’s thickness (31 cm in all), the hit lasts 54 ms and pushes with about 3.14 MN. A perfectly rigid body would make the force infinite, but relativity forbids one: no push travels through a body faster than light. Even the stiffest body physics allows takes 2.1 ns to stop, which limits the average force to about 25.9 TN.
math: Charge: his sprint after a 28.7 m run-up → v = 18.1 m/s; momentum p = γ m v = 54,400 kg·m/s. A charger who takes his own recoil doesn’t slow, so he acts as a body of unbounded mass at speed v. In his frame Rex arrives at v and meets an immovable body: a splat stops Rex against him, so in the ground frame Rex leaves with him at v; a perfect bounce sends Rex back at v in his frame, so in the ground frame Rex leaves at v′ = 2v/(1 + v²/c²) (relativistic velocity addition: c tanh 2w, w his rapidity). Momentum Rex gains: γ m v (splat) or 2γ² m v (bounce), here 109,000 kg·m/s. Ollie’s source supplies it, plus what Rex’s footing hands the ground during the hit (its hold, at most the hit’s force, × the hit’s time; none in the bounce bound): 109,000 kg·m/s. Energy freed in a splat: Rex’s motion energy in Ollie’s frame, (γ − 1) m c² (½ m v² below 1% of light speed) = 494 kJ. Force: squash s = ½ × the smaller depth = 31 cm; F = Q/s (splat) or 2Q/s peak (bounce). Ordinary solids and liquids at everyday pressures can’t carry sound faster than about 36 km/s; nothing travels faster than light, which limits the average force. Run-up: m u du/dx = T − k u², so u = u_top √(1 − e^(−2kx/m)) over x = 28.7 m, capped by his legs. Slide: x = m/(2k)·ln(1 + kV²/R), k = ½ρ₀C_dA. Blast radii: Kinney & Graham (1985), as if all of Q became a blast (upper bound). Quake: 1 part in 10,000 of Q (the usual share, give or take ⅔ of a magnitude), as if all of Q reached the ground, which overstates it. Ollie’s horns don’t change the momentum or the energy; they only put the force on a smaller patch.

set.verdict: Ollie hits Rex at 300 km/s and doesn’t slow: he takes his own recoil, so the push back from the hit goes to his source. Rex is carried along at 300 km/s. When Ollie stops, at the end of the squash, Rex slides 9.15 km before he stops.

happens: Momentum still balances, and canon says where it comes from. Ollie doesn’t slow, so everything Rex gains (899 million kg·m/s), and what his footing hands the ground during the hit (0.037 kg·m/s), comes from Ollie’s source: about 900 million kg·m/s in all. That is canon’s case “their own recoil”: the push back from his own hit goes to his source. A splat frees Rex’s motion energy as Ollie sees it (below).“Immovable” only means what holds Rex in place. Against a charger who can’t slow, any hold with a limit gives: here his footing, 17.7 kN. Only a hold their powers make limitless can’t give (bolts on ground that Unbreakable footing keeps whole, or Unbreakable footing holding him up from below), and then there is no answer.How far Ollie carries him is up to Ollie: he never slows, so he could push on for as long as he likes. The lab ends the carry at the end of the squash, 2.1 µs in: Ollie stops himself there (his own push, so its push back, 899 million kg·m/s, goes to his source too), and Rex slides on from 300 km/s.The hit frees 135 TJ (32 kt TNT): Rex’s motion energy as Ollie sees it. Canon: a hit’s freed energy is taken back by default (it shows as his shimmer, which the lab doesn’t draw yet) and is real only when he means it. The lab reads a blast preset (rattle the windows, break windows, flatten houses, a block) as meaning it.How hard they hit depends on how squishy they are, which nobody knows for an indestructible plush. If they squash by a quarter of the smaller body’s thickness (31 cm in all), the hit lasts 2.1 µs and pushes with about 429 TN. A perfectly rigid body would make the force infinite, but relativity forbids one: no push travels through a body faster than light. Even the stiffest body physics allows takes 2.1 ns to stop, which limits the average force to about 429 PN.The push still goes into the ground under Rex. Carried along, his footing hands the ground what it held during the hit: 0.037 kg·m/s over 64 ms (it reaches the ground through his legs, which spread it over at least a stamp’s contact time, an estimate). That shakes the ground as real physics says: too little to feel.

Relativity forbids one, so the hit is never infinite.Momentum still balances, and canon says where it comes from. Ollie doesn’t slow, so everything Rex gains (49,700 kg·m/s), and what the ground under him takes during the hit (49,700 kg·m/s), comes from Ollie’s source: about 99,000 kg·m/s in all. That is canon’s case “their own recoil”: the push back from his own hit goes to his source. A splat frees Rex’s motion energy as Ollie sees it (below).“Immovable” only means what holds Rex in place. Against a charger who can’t slow, any hold with a limit gives: here the ground under his feet, which bears 1.52 MN on the concrete slab. Only a hold their powers make limitless can’t give (bolts on ground that Unbreakable footing keeps whole, or Unbreakable footing holding him up from below), and then there is no answer. The plush squash alone pushes with only 1.31 MN, less than that, but Ollie can’t slow, so the push rises until it gives. The lab’s figures for the hit are the squash’s, so here they are rough.Unbreakable footing is off here, so the ground under Rex is real: driven down at Ollie’s speed, he goes in as the lab drives any landing in (its penetration model, an estimate). Ollie never slows, so the lab has him stop himself as the hit ends (his own push, its push back to his source).The hit frees 412 kJ (98 g TNT): Rex’s motion energy as Ollie sees it. Canon: a hit’s freed energy is taken back by default (it shows as his shimmer, which the lab doesn’t draw yet) and is real only when he means it. The lab reads a blast preset (rattle the windows, break windows, flatten houses, a block) as meaning it.How hard they hit depends on how squishy they are, which nobody knows for an indestructible plush. If they squash by a quarter of the smaller body’s thickness (31 cm in all), the hit lasts 38 ms and pushes with about 1.31 MN. A perfectly rigid body would make the force infinite, but relativity forbids one: no push travels through a body faster than light. The physics above is less sure.Show the mathCharge: falling from his 14 m jump → v = 16.6 m/s; momentum p = γ m v = 49,700 kg·m/s. A charger who takes his own recoil doesn’t slow, so he acts as a body of unbounded mass at speed v. In his frame Rex arrives at v and meets an immovable body: a splat stops Rex against him, so in the ground frame Rex leaves with him at v; a perfect bounce sends Rex back at v in his frame, so in the ground frame Rex leaves at v′ = 2v/(1 + v²/c²) (relativistic velocity addition: c tanh 2w, w his rapidity). Momentum Rex gains: γ m v (splat) or 2γ² m v (bounce), here 49,700 kg·m/s. Ollie’s source supplies it, plus what Rex’s footing hands the ground during the hit (its hold, at most the hit’s force, × the hit’s time; none in the bounce bound): 99,400 kg·m/s. Energy freed in a splat: Rex’s motion energy in Ollie’s frame, (γ − 1) m c² (½ m v² below 1% of light speed) = 412 kJ. Force: squash s = ½ × the smaller depth = 31 cm; F = Q/s (splat) or 2Q/s peak (bounce). Ordinary solids and liquids at everyday pressures can’t carry sound faster than about 36 km/s; nothing travels faster than light, which limits the average force. Slide: x = m/(2k)·ln(1 + kV²/R), k = ½ρ₀C_dA. Blast radii: Kinney & Graham (1985), as if all of Q became a blast (upper bound). Quake: 1 part in 10,000 of Q (the usual share, give or take ⅔ of a magnitude), as if all of Q reached the ground, which overstates it. Ollie’s horns don’t change the momentum or the energy; they only put the force on a smaller patch.
